assays.assay_description: Working memory assessed by spontaneous alternation in a T-maze. After 5-min training the day before, mice are placed at the cross section and freely choose right or left arm (8 repetitions); percentage of correct alternation is measured.

application_type.evidence: treated with 0.05 mg/kg body weight (BW) psilocybin by oral gavage

setup_habituation.evidence: After a 5-minute training inside the T-maze, performed the day before the test

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed at the cross section and left free to decide to explore the right or the left arm

food_restriction.evidence: Standard short test apparatus with no food present during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard short test apparatus with no water present during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: Timing between last dose and T-maze test not specified.

sample_size.evidence: Sample size for the T-maze not explicitly reported in the figure legend.

outcomes.summary: No significant effect of psilocybin on percentage of correct alternation in the T-maze, although median value in controls and psilocybin-treated mice (86%) was higher than in HFHFD mice (71%).
outcomes.evidence: No significant effect was observed on the percentage of correct alternation in the T-maze test, although the median value in healthy controls and psilocybin treated mice was higher than that of HFHFD mice (86 % for healthy controls and psilocybin-treated, vs 71 % for HFHFD-fed mice).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Only percentage of spontaneous alternation reported.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Single percentage per animal; no within-session time course.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural sequences or transitions.

B4_ethological.evidence: Working memory choice measure; not a natural ethological behaviour.

B5_social.evidence: Animal tested alone; no social construct.

B6_cognitive.evidence: The T-maze test was performed to assess the eventual effects of the diet or the treatment on the working memory.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: No pose-estimation or ML behavioural classifier mentioned.

E2_shelter.evidence: T-maze arms are not enclosed shelters.

E6_spatial.evidence: right or the left arm of the T-maze

E7_social_context.evidence: mice were placed at the cross section

E8_food_water.evidence: No food/water in apparatus during test.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Exact test duration not stated; 8 repetitions consistent with short test.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Single test day; prior day was training without data reported.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline T-maze recording reported.

assays.assay_description: Anxiety-like behaviour test; mice placed in the light compartment of an LDB chamber and allowed to move freely between light and dark compartments. Measures: total time in light, immobility in light, latency to enter dark compartment.

setup_habituation.evidence: No habituation to LDB apparatus described.

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to move freely between the two areas

food_restriction.evidence: Standard short anxiety test with no food in apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard short anxiety test with no water in apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: Interval between last dose and LDB test not specified.

sample_size.evidence: n = 8 [healthy controls and HFHFD], n = 10 [HFHFD + psilocybin]

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin increased the latency to first enter the dark compartment, suggesting a potential anti-anxiety effect. No significant differences were observed in total time in light or immobility time.
outcomes.evidence: The light-dark box test showed that time before entering the dark chamber was increased by psilocybin treatment, suggesting a potential anti-anxiety effect (Fig. 1G).

B1_num_measures.evidence: total time spent in the light compartment (LC), immobility time in the LC and latency to enter into the dark compartment (DC)

B4_ethological.evidence: Zone preference time is a spatial measure, not an ethological behaviour.

B5_social.evidence: Anxiety test with no social component.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Light-Dark Box is a standard apparatus.

E2_shelter.evidence: Fully enclosed dark compartment serves as refuge.

D1_continuity.evidence: Single LDB test session per animal.

D5_followup.evidence: LDB performed during ongoing chronic dosing, not as post-acute follow-up after cessation.

assays.assay_description: Mouse placed in centre of a square metal grid which is then inverted; hanging time recorded. After fall, mouse returned and trial repeated until first sign of weakness or up to 10 min. Outcomes: grid score (BW * time), time on grid, time of first fall. Performed at 6, 8, 10, and 12 weeks of treatment.

setup_habituation.evidence: No habituation to the grid apparatus described.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mouse hangs freely on inverted grid; no restraint.

food_restriction.evidence: Standard short test with no food in apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard short test with no water in apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: performed after 6, 8, 10 and 12 weeks of pharmacological treatment

sample_size.evidence: Sample sizes for grid test not explicitly stated in figure legend.

outcomes.summary: HFHFD reduced grid score, time on grid, and time of first fall. Psilocybin-treated HFHFD mice maintained better performance on all three measures across 6, 8, 10, and 12 weeks of treatment.
outcomes.evidence: HFHFD-fed mice treated with psilocybin maintained better performances at the grid test compared to HFHFD-fed vehicle-treated mice.

B1_num_measures.evidence: total time spent on the grid normalized per animal body weight (score), the time spent on the grid and the time of the first fall from the grid

B4_ethological.evidence: Muscle strength performance test, not ethological.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Square metal grid is a standard apparatus.

E7_social_context.evidence: The mouse was placed in the center of a square metal grid.

D1_continuity.evidence: performed after 6, 8, 10 and 12 weeks of pharmacological treatment

D2_session_duration.evidence: session was repeated till the first sign of weakness or distress, and no longer than 10 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Grid test performed at 4 timepoints (6, 8, 10, 12 weeks).

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline grid test reported (treatment began at week 5).

D5_followup.evidence: All grid testing occurred during ongoing chronic dosing, not >=24h after cessation of treatment.

judge_notes: Three behavioural assays scored: T-maze (working memory), Light-Dark Box (anxiety), and Grid test (muscle strength). All other endpoints (histology, transcriptomics, lipidomics, ipGTT, electron microscopy, in vitro cell assays) are non-behavioural and not scored.
Grid test D1/D3 scored as multiple sessions across 6/8/10/12 weeks per figure 8 legend; candidate gpt-oss missed this. D2 capped at <15 min (max 10 min stated explicitly).
D5 (post-acute follow-up) scored 0 for all assays: behavioural testing occurred during ongoing chronic dosing (5 days/week), not >=24h after cessation, per the rubric's intent.
B5 set to 'None' for T-maze, LDB, and Grid — these are not social-cognition constructs; gpt-oss's score of 1 was overruled.
Housing fields kept as not_reported per silence in methods (light cycle direction unspecified beyond '12-h alternating').
